project.name: Commander Simulator Platform
project.description: Import Commander decklists, convert to Forge's .dck format, batch-simulate pods via Forge's headless CLI sim mode, parse results and detect turning points, and present them in a web dashboard.
project.scope_boundary: Single local user, Commander format only, batch simulation (not interactive play), no auth/hosting concerns.

engine.name: Forge
engine.vendoring: git submodule at engine/forge, pinned to a specific commit (see engine/forge-pin.txt)
engine.java_version: 17 (project targets maven.compiler.release=17; JDK 21 used here builds it fine)

cli_flags.-d: one or more deck files/names, in player order
cli_flags.-D: absolute directory to load decks from (alternative to -d)
cli_flags.-n: number of games (default 1) - spec default below is 20
cli_flags.-m: play a full match of N games instead of -n (not used; we run independent games, not a match)
cli_flags.-s: RNG seed (optional, useful for reproducing a specific game)
cli_flags.-a: AI profile per player (optional; default AI used unless we later want to compare AI configs)
cli_flags.-c: per-game clock in seconds before it's called a draw; Forge default is 120 - likely needs raising for 4-player Commander games and will be tuned empirically in Phase 0/2
cli_flags.-q: quiet: only emit match-result lines, not the full log. We do NOT use this flag, since Phase 3 needs the full per-game log to parse.

engine.output: stdout: per-game log lines (forge.game.GameLogEntry.toString()) followed by a 'Game Result: ...' summary line per game
known_risks: AI may stall on complex board states; -c clock exists as a safety valve, tune the timeout empirically
Card resolution: a specific printing referenced by an imported deck may not exist in Forge's card database

deck_format.commander_section_note: Exactly one (or two, for partner commanders) card(s) in [Commander]; the rest of the 99 in [Main]. Confirmed against Forge's own bundled Commander precons at forge-gui/res/adventure/common/decks/starter/commander/*.dck
deck_format.example_source_used_for_validation: forge-gui/res/adventure/common/decks/starter/commander/red_01.dck (vendored inside the Forge submodule, not duplicated in this repo)

moxfield.status: CONFIRMED against a real live deck (user-supplied JSON from api2.moxfield.com/v3/decks/all/{publicId}); see PROGRESS.md Phase 1
moxfield.api_note: Moxfield has an undocumented public JSON API used by its own web client. boards.{commanders,mainboard,sideboard}.cards is Record<string, {quantity, card: {name, set, cn, ...}}> - confirmed exactly as implemented. MDFCs report a combined 'Front // Back' name; truncated to front face in server/src/convert/dck.ts since that's how Forge indexes them.
moxfield.input_shape_expected: a Moxfield deck URL, e.g. https://www.moxfield.com/decks/<publicId>
moxfield.normalization_target: internal NormalizedDeck shape (see data_model.NormalizedDeck) decoupled from Moxfield's response shape

archidekt.status: DEPRIORITIZED BY USER - user confirmed Moxfield is their actual deck source; Archidekt import is out of scope until asked for again. See PROGRESS.md.
archidekt.input_shape_expected: an Archidekt deck URL, e.g. https://archidekt.com/decks/<id>

stages: resolve (NormalizedDeck card entries -> a concrete Forge printing per card; fallback: match by name if exact set/collector-number printing isn't in Forge's DB)
simulate (invoke Forge sim CLI with 4 .dck files)
parse (raw stdout log -> structured per-game event list + result)
analyze (event list -> turning points, per spec.turning_point_signals)

simulation_defaults.seed_strategy: unseeded by default for a batch (each game independently random); support an optional fixed seed per game for reproducing/debugging one specific game

log_parsing.input: Forge sim-mode stdout: a sequence of GameLogEntry lines per game, then a 'Game Result: ...' summary line
log_parsing.target_shape: per game: { gameIndex, durationMs, players[], events[], winner, isDraw }, events[] = { turn, index, type, raw, players_involved[] } at minimum
log_parsing.note: Forge's GameLogEntryType enum (in forge-game) is the authoritative list of log line categories; use it to classify lines rather than re-inventing categories from scratch.

turning_point_signals.note: Seed list per task instructions. Explicitly expected to be refined once real logs are in hand (see PRD.md risk #4) - this is a starting hypothesis, not a final taxonomy.

signals.description: A mass-removal effect destroys/exiles multiple creatures across multiple players in one event.
signals.heuristic: log line(s) indicating a spell/ability that matches 'destroys all' / 'each player sacrifices' / similar, followed by multiple creatures leaving the battlefield in the same step.

signals.description: A single event changes a player's life total by a large margin (damage burst, big lifegain, or a life-loss payment).
signals.heuristic: life total delta for one player >= 10 in a single log step.

signals.description: A player is removed from the game (loses).
signals.heuristic: GameLogEntryType for a player loss / MATCH_RESULTS entry naming a player as having lost mid-game.

signals.description: A commander is cast from the command zone, especially a recast paying commander tax after a prior removal.
signals.heuristic: a cast event whose source is a card also present in that player's [Commander] section, cross-referenced against prior commander-zone-change events for the same card.

signals.description: A player takes an additional turn.
signals.heuristic: a turn-structure log event indicating an extra turn granted, or two turn entries in a row for the same player.

signals.description: Multiple lands are destroyed in one event, across one or more players.
signals.heuristic: multiple land permanents leaving the battlefield via destroy/sacrifice in the same step.

signals.description: A player draws an unusually large number of cards in one event.
signals.heuristic: a draw event of >= 5 cards for one player in a single step.

signals.description: A repeating near-identical sequence of log lines suggests an infinite/combo loop being resolved (or the sim clock cutting it off).
signals.heuristic: the same (source, ability) pair repeating >= N times in a short window of consecutive steps.

signals.description: Combat damage in a single combat step reduces a player to 0 or below (the finishing blow).
signals.heuristic: a combat-damage log step whose target player's resulting life <= 0.

signals.description: A spell is countered that would otherwise have been a large mana-value/impactful play.
signals.heuristic: a counter event whose countered spell has mana value >= 5 (threshold to revisit once real data is seen).

CardRef.name: string
CardRef.setCode: string | null (as reported by the source; may not resolve to a real Forge printing)

GameResult.rawLog: string (full stdout for this game, kept for re-parsing if the parser improves)

tech_stack.storage: flat JSON files under data/runs/<run-id>.json (see PROGRESS.md decisions - deviated from an original SQLite plan since a single-writer, read-mostly, one-file-per-run shape didn't need a database)
tech_stack.rationale: single language across import pipeline/API/UI, minimal operational overhead for a local single-user tool

phases.name: Moxfield import -> normalized decklist -> .dck

phases.name: Log parsing + turning-point detection
